statement: Within the same neighbourhood and day, NYC hyperlocal sensors with more street trees nearby record lower afternoon air temperature.

graph_evidence.summary: Satellite surface temperature tracks ground air temperature (r about 0.9; R2 0.9).

graph_evidence.relationship_id: (concepts I2CN3brExA tree, lHLIKbfnYp green space, RF7tCwCaa5 vegetation cover)
graph_evidence.summary: The tree concept has no relationships. Green space has 14, none with temperature, heat illness or emergency care. Surface temperature links only to air temperature (r about 0.9, 2 studies), population density (r 0.82) and deforestation (r 0.89). No finding connects trees or green space to heat-related ED visits.

literature.citation: Ziter CD, Pedersen EJ, Kucharik CJ, Turner MG. Scale-dependent interactions between tree canopy cover and impervious surfaces reduce daytime urban heat during summer. PNAS 2019;116:7575-7580.
literature.finding: Bicycle-transect air temperatures in Madison: daytime air temperature falls with canopy cover, nonlinearly, with the largest cooling above about 40% canopy at 60-90 m scales.

prediction.magnitude: Per 10 additional live street trees within 50 m of a sensor, mean 12:00-18:00 air temperature lower by 0.05 to 0.5 C, within NTA-by-day.
prediction.support_if: slope negative with upper 95% limit (sensor-clustered SE) below 0
prediction.refute_if: slope positive with lower limit above 0

plan: Data: Hyperlocal Temperature Monitoring (qdq3-9eqn), summers 2018 and 2019, sensor-day mean airtemp over hours 12-18 via SoQL group by sensor_id, day; sensor coordinates, install_type and ntacode. Trees: 2015 Street Tree Census live trees with coordinates (uvpi-gqnh), counted within 50 m (and 100 m, sensitivity) of each sensor using projected coordinates. Model: OLS of sensor-day afternoon temperature on trees50/10 and install_type, with NTA-by-day fixed effects (comparisons only among sensors in the same NTA on the same day); SE clustered by sensor. Report the slope in C per 10 trees.
alternatives: Sensor siting: sensors on light poles vs trees differ in shade and height (install_type is controlled)
Trees cluster on residential side streets, away from wide arterial roads and heat from traffic
The 2015 census predates the 2018-2019 readings; plantings and removals in between add noise
